canada.title: $200K from N.L. going to downtown St. John’s for private security foot patrols
canada.summary: On Thursday Newfoundland and Labrador’s justice minister announced $200,000 in funding to boost safety in downtown St. John’s, which is going towards uniformed foot patrols. Downtown St. John’s chair Jonathan Loder says it will act as a deterrent against crime.

canada.title: Province to install ‘City of Champions’ signs on highways into Edmonton
canada.summary: After a historic Grey Cup victory for the Edmonton Elks, questions whirled around about whether the city should reinstate the “City of Champions” slogan on its welcome sign. Alberta’s Transportation Minister, Devin Dreeshen, says he wants to make that happen.

canada.title: Housing project in Brossard, Que., promised affordability. Residents said no
canada.summary: The City of Brossard is asking a developer to go back to the drawing board after a group of residents blocked a housing project that would have brought 810 units, including affordable housing, to the city's edge.

canada.title: Better ministerial reporting could grow Albertans' confidence in how tax dollars are spent: auditor general
canada.summary: Alberta’s auditor general says he believes provincial ministries could make improvements to how they report on their achievements, and that doing so could increase public trust in how the government is performing.

canada.title: They finally had their dream food truck. Then it was repossessed
canada.summary: A family ran their business, LeoMay Fusion, out of a food truck for about a year in rural Nova Scotia until RCMP officers showed up in mid-October and they learned a previous lender was repossessing the vehicle.

canada.title: Province in talks with Quebec-based company about idled Nackawic pulp mill
canada.summary: The AV Group stopped production at its Nackawic pulp mill in early November, but Natural Resources Minister John Herron told the legislature Friday that he’s hopeful the province can find another operator.

canada.title: New federal ‘digital transformation’ chief says he took the job for $1 a year

canada.title: Ontario fugitive arrested in Winnipeg hours after making most wanted list
canada.summary: An Ontario fugitive wanted in connection with two Toronto-area shootings was arrested in Winnipeg Thursday, less than six hours after being placed on Canada’s most wanted list.

canada.title: Transport truck driver charged after rollerblader struck and killed in Ajax: police
canada.summary: A driver is facing charges after a rollerblader was struck and killed by a transport truck in Ajax earlier this year.

canada.title: N.B. RCMP are investigating preterm fetus remains found in an airport bathroom
canada.summary: Police say they're investigating the circumstances surrounding the discovery of the remains and provided no further details.

canada.title: Silver Alert cancelled after missing 76-year-old Winnipeg man located
canada.summary: A missing 76-year-old man who was the subject of a Silver Alert has been found and is safe, Winnipeg police say.

canada.title: Dozens gather at Yukon legislature building to protest end of rent control, return of no-cause evictions
canada.summary: About 50 people gathered outside the Jim Smith building in Whitehorse on Thursday, protesting recent amendments to the territory’s Residential Tenancies Act which removed the rent cap and brought back no-cause evictions.

canada.summary: NDP submission argues Nova Scotia Power shareholders should shoulder the costs.

canada.title: B.C. premier to be sworn in, announce cabinet at Government House
canada.summary: Lorne Doerkson will be sworn in on Friday as B.C.'s 38th premier by Lt.-Gov. Wendy Cocchia, alongside his cabinet.

canada.title: Tumbler Ridge shooter used ChatGPT to build 3D gun parts, U.S. magazine reports
canada.summary: Mother Jones reports that ChatGPT helped killer Jesse Van Rootselaar make a 3D-printed gun magazine and foregrip, and gave advice on how to fix a spring, before the deadly mass shooting on Feb. 10.

canada.title: Historic guns locked away as RCMP centre set to become next national museum
